verdict.headline: Exploratory screen: allocator-first loop and single-lock allocation pass all 17 correctness gates with 1.44% disk latency gain, within noise.

blocks.text: No upstream comparison has been measured.

sections.title: Eliminating redundant operations on synchronous cold swap-in
sections.lead: Synchronous swapin repeats a cache lookup after callers miss, and __swap_cache_alloc acquires ci->lock twice for order-0 faults. Candidate exp1-sync-zero-redundancy-v1 removes both redundant operations.

blocks.text: Hypothesis 1 combines allocator-first reordering in swapin_sync() with single-lock order-0 allocation in __swap_cache_alloc(). Evaluated under Protocol Revision 7 with attributable metadata accounting.

sections.title: System architecture of synchronous swap-in
sections.lead: Faulting tasks traverse swap cache lookup, folio allocation, swap cache entry publication, and backing storage read.

blocks.takeaway: Synchronous fault path flows from page fault to backing store completion

sections.title: Swap cache allocation and publication path
sections.lead: Baseline performs unpinned lock and lookup, memory allocation, and authoritative locked validation. Candidate removes preliminary locking for order-0 demand faults.

blocks.takeaway: Single lock acquisition protects publication while preserving slot validation

sections.title: Allocator-first reordering and single-lock order-0 allocation
sections.lead: Reordered swapin_sync calls __swap_cache_alloc_folio first, handling -EEXIST via cache lookup fallback. Preliminary cluster lock check omitted for order-0 demand faults.

blocks.takeaway: Order-0 cold path avoids duplicate lookup and preliminary lock acquisition

blocks.x_label: Metadata bytes per 1,000 capacity slots (baseline only)
blocks.note: Valid calibration samples; candidate performance was not measured here.

sections.title: Next steps: profile-bound architectural decision
sections.lead: Fast screening benchmark demonstrated full correctness across all 17 gates and a modest 1.44% sequential disk swapin latency gain. Because gain is below the 5% min_useful_effect policy threshold and within noise, candidate is retained as an exploratory screen.

blocks.text: The candidate proves that single-lock allocation and allocator-first loops are functionally correct and lockdep-safe. Exploration may focus on batched or asynchronous prefetch mechanisms.
